claim: Hoge Kempen National Park has six current gateways: Terhills (Maasmechelen), Mechelse Heide (Maasmechelen), Kattevennen (Genk), Pietersheim (Lanaken), Lieteberg (Zutendaal), and Station As (As).
quote: Terhills (formerly Connecterra, Maasmechelen) is the main gateway, where the National Park Visitor Center is located. Mechelse Heide... Kattevennen in Genk... Pietersheim in Lanaken... The Lieteberg in Zutendaal... Station As in As.

claim: Terhills (formerly Connecterra) is the main gateway with the National Park Visitor Centre, sitting on the former Eisden coal mine site that closed in 1987; loop walks from 1.4 to 10.9 km depart from it, and three of four terrils are climbable.
quote: Terhills is the former Eisden mine site. When the mine closed in 1987, the area was remediated... Various loop-shaped routes start at the Visitors Centre, with distances from 1.4 km to 10.9 km. Terhills has 4 terrils, 3 of which are accessible.

claim: The Mechelse Heide gateway in Maasmechelen offers seven hiking loops from the main entrance plus extra loops from Station Eisden and Kikmolen campsite, with the 1.5 km wheelchair-accessible Zandloperpad as a key feature.
quote: The gateway provides access to seven hiking loops starting directly from the main entrance... Zandloperpad (Sandpiper Path): A 1.5-kilometer paved wheelchair-accessible track.

claim: The Mechelse Heide panorama point is the highest spot in the National Park at 104 m above sea level, reached via a 7.3 km red-triangle loop with views to the former mining terrils on clear days.
quote: The panorama point is the highest point in the National Park, located 104 meters above sea level. A recommended red triangle walk is 7.3 km with pleasant height differences and a spectacular panorama point.

claim: Terhills offers colour-coded trails including a 4 km green route to Panorama Ridge with two viewpoints, a 9.6 km red route across the long and double terril, and a 14.1 km yellow route over the pontoon bridge.
quote: The 4 km green route takes you to the top of the Panorama Ridge with 2 beautiful viewpoints. The red route of 9.6 km... The yellow route of 14.1 km is Terhills' longest walk.

claim: The Terhills resort area combines the Terhills Hotel (four-star, 59 rooms), Terhills Resort cottages, Elaisa Energetic Wellness, the Terhills Cablepark for waterskiing/wakeboarding, an Aqua Garden, adventure golf, jeep safari and bike rental.
quote: Terhills Cablepark for water sports at all skill levels; Elaisa Energetic Wellness featuring spa and relaxation services; Aqua Garden... Terhills Hotel (59 four-star rooms); Adventure Golf; Jeep Safari experiences.

claim: Elaisa Energetic Wellness at Terhills is themed around crystals, natural materials and ancient cultures (Maya, Inca, Egyptian) and sits roughly 200 m from the Terhills Resort cottages.
quote: Elaisa Energetic Wellness welcomes you to a true oasis of tranquillity... surrounded by beautiful Terhills nature with geometric shapes, crystals and natural materials, along with influences from ancient world cultures such as the Maya, Incas and Egyptians.

claim: The 'Cycling between Terrils' route at Terhills features a floating pontoon bridge nearly 380 m long that carries cyclists and pedestrians over the water with 360-degree views of the former mining landscape.
quote: A unique cycling route links the iconic mine heaps (terrils) of the former Eisden coal mine with a floating pontoon bridge spanning nearly 380 metres, carrying cyclists and pedestrians right above the water's surface, offering a full 360-degree view.

claim: Maasmechelen Village designer outlet is open every day 10:00–19:00 including Sundays, year-round except 25 December and 1 January.
quote: The village operates daily from 10:00 – 19:00, including Sundays. As stated on the page, 'The Village is open every day of the week all year long except 25 December and 1 January.'

claim: The Pietersheim gateway in Lanaken centres on a 12th-century Romanesque 'Waterburcht' water castle within a 76-hectare estate, with a visitors' lounge, petting zoo, floating walkway and eight signposted hiking loops (four starting at the castle).
quote: The former royal estate 'Pietersheim' covers 76 hectares and features the 12th-century 'Waterburcht' (water castle)... The 'Pietersheim' hiking area boasts eight signposted hiking loops, four of which start at the entrance gate.

claim: From autumn through Easter the Waterburcht at Pietersheim is only accessible with a guide; outside that period it can be visited freely, and the visitor car park sits a 5-minute walk away.
quote: From autumn to Easter holidays, the Castle of Water is only accessible with a guide, while outside this period, you are free to visit during opening hours.

claim: E-bike rental is available at the National Park Visitor Centre in Terhills/Maasmechelen (Zetellaan 54) and at Domein Pietersheim in Lanaken, which keeps 6 city bikes, 6 e-bikes and 2 tandems from Easter through autumn holidays.
quote: At the National Park Hoge Kempen Visitor Center in Maasmechelen... you can rent electric bikes... At Domein Pietersheim in Lanaken, you can rent bikes from Easter holidays to autumn holidays, with options including 6 city bikes, 6 e-bikes, and 2 tandems.

claim: Lanaken sits on the cycling 'knooppunten' (numbered junction) network at the Belgian–Dutch border with over 60 km of dedicated cycle paths; the Pietersheim access point lies between junctions 131 and 140.
quote: Lanaken is perfectly located on the border between Belgian and Dutch Limburg for cycling adventures, offering more than 60 kilometres of cycling paths... At the Pietersheim access point in Lanaken, located between cycling junctions 131 and 140.

claim: Hoge Kempen, established in 2006, is Belgium's first and only national park, covering roughly 12,000 ha across Maasmechelen, Lanaken, Dilsen-Stokkem, Zutendaal, Genk and As.
